seen.where: Gallica microfilm of BnF italien 1590, ark btv1b10037390v, read through openapi.bnf.fr IIIF on 11 Nov 2026: view 393 (f. 392 recto, full and a 1500 px crop), view 394 (f. 392 verso and f. 393), view 286 (f. 285), views 284-285 (ff. 283-284)
seen.extent: f. 392: one small leaf, 13 lines of cipher (roughly 450-500 signs) after the single clear word 'Signore.', with a clear dating line 'dat[um] ut in l[itte]ris', '8 Sept[embris]' and the signature 'Idem servus Antonius'. f. 285 (the other piece of the lead) is a slip of 6 cipher lines.
seen.cipher: f. 392: a symbol cipher of the Sforza chancery type (letters, digit-like signs and signs with strokes and superscript marks, written continuously with no word division). No decipherment is written on the recto; the verso (view 394, left) shows only show-through and one faded word by the seal stain. The leaf that follows, f. 393, is Trezzo's long clear despatch of the same day ('1464. 8 7bris', beginning 'Illustrissimo signore mio. Grandissima letitia ha dimonstrato la Maesta del S. Re ...'), far longer than the slip, so it is the covering letter and not a translation of it. f. 285 differs: there every cipher line carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment ('questa novella e stata cazata da Brochardo ...', '... tagliato la testa ...', '... suspicione ...'), so f. 285 is read on the leaf and only f. 392 is open.
